In one of my newsletters I covered the tactics on zero-budget growth

#1 there was "use AI to reduce execution costs"

Most people use AI for content (contAInt meh). And they use it very wrong because they focus on increasing the output instead of increasing the quality.

You can literally use AI for data analysis, scraping, generating 100 hook ideas, creating customer avatars, vibecoding side products for your main business, social listening, turning your voice notes into content ideas...

But you chose to delegate the full content-production cycle to AI.
The part in which it's probably worst.

For me it's not about writing actually.
Many of my posts are written with AI and then proofread.
But I never let AI create something from scratch.

AI is your intern.
Let it do the intern work.

PS: If you haven't had a chance to read my piece on zero marketing budget growth, here's the link; you'll love it ↓

https://t.co/3vR20mOqzG

tweets.text:
AI stocks have sold off over the past few days.

The main drivers: hotter-than-expected US inflation (Sept CPI 3.7% YoY) raising the odds of further Fed hikes, plus growing worries about the cost of financing the massive AI infrastructure buildout. Heavily leveraged names like CoreWeave (roughly $50B in debt/obligations) have been hit especially hard, with bond yields spiking toward 15-16% and credit spreads flashing stress.

Yet the demand picture looks different. Cloud GPU rental prices for high-end chips remain elevated and in several cases, are still trending higher - a real-time signal that compute demand is tight. 

Meanwhile, OpenAI and Anthropic continue scaling: Anthropic just reported $16.8B in Q3 revenue (+45% QoQ), +ve FCF and adjusted profitability, while OpenAI’s net annualised run rate sits around $50B with strong enterprise growth.

This looks more like a rates-and-financing-driven valuation reset than a collapse in underlying AI demand. For investors who believe the secular compute story remains intact, these pullbacks can create selective opportunities - particularly in higher-quality names.
https://t.co/YKr5pL7G2c

tweets.text: A note to young men (those under 50). Enjoy your youth. From my perspective, I hit a physical high around 2010 at age 35. There is a reason why no great sports heros are in their 50s. You peak as a man from a physical perspective in your 30s. You just do. That does not mean the 30s should be a pinnacle of life. Indeed, life really just gets going in one’s 40s. The 50s are good too. But as someone in their 50s, I am not looking forward to my 60s or 70s. Why? B/c I can already feel my body weakening and no matter what I do, it will never be what it was in my 30s40s. This is why even guys like Tom Brady have to retire. Father Time is undefeated. 50s and 60s can be really fun, but a man in his 30s is total alpha.

These are the most important charts on X and in the market. One year ago, I said the S&P was escaping a channel that went back 100 years. It did exactly that. Then in March, it checked right back down to it and rebounded. It is in a new channel now. One that should take it to around 10,000 by the end of next year.

Stop playing the days and weeks, play the months.

First chart below shows the original channel I posted about last October. The second chart shows that channel, overlaid with a secondary channel that started at the '87-crash low, along with the new channel that began at the tariff-low last year. 

It is steeper and reflects the inflationary nature of S&P earnings, the passive-inflow effect, the defined-contribution effect, and the general resiliency that now exists in US stocks given their position as America's retirement and tax revenue (cap gains).

Sell stocks at your own peril.

Things are about to really go parabolic.
